name: Classical Median-Graph Equivalence
hypotheses: Finite connected graph; the forbidden-minor and majority formulations use a partial-cube representation.
statement: The unique-median, hypercube-retract, CAT(0) cubical, two-obstruction, convex-expansion, and majority-closed formulations define the same class.
proof: The first five equivalences are the classical results assembled in the source theorem. For a median partial cube, the unique vertex in the three pairwise intervals has, in every coordinate, the majority bit of the triple. Conversely, closure under coordinatewise majority supplies that unique common interval vertex for every triple.
